title: How to Cancel The Athletic Without Missing a Separate Charge (2026)
metaDescription: Cancel The Athletic through its account settings, an NYT account, Apple, or Google Play. Check for a separate subscription before you finish.
intro: The Athletic can appear inside a New York Times bundle and still have a separate standalone subscription. Before cancelling anything, open the receipt and identify whether NYTimes, Apple, or Google Play processed the payment.

heroImage.alt: Football supporters outside Anfield stadium after a match
heroImage.caption: Football supporters leaving Anfield. The Athletic subscription itself is managed by the account or app store shown on the receipt. Image resized for web use.

steps.title: Match the charge to its billing channel
steps.text: Check the receipt and the Subscription Overview in your New York Times account. The overview should direct you to the place that manages the subscription.
steps.tip: Look for a standalone Athletic plan even if your current NYT plan already includes Athletic access. They can be separate purchases.

image.alt: New York Times Help Center account-management guidance for The Athletic
image.caption: The current help page says the Subscription Overview directs each Athletic customer to the right account-management location.
image.sourceLabel: The New York Times Help Center

steps.title: Cancel a standalone Athletic subscription
steps.text: Open nytimes.com/athletic/settings while signed in to the paying account. Follow the cancellation option and review the date on which paid access ends.
steps.tip: The New York Times terms also allow Athletic subscribers to contact customer support when the account page does not resolve the charge.

steps.title: Manage an NYT bundle in the NYT account
steps.text: If The Athletic is included in All Access or Home Delivery, use the New York Times account area to manage the bundle. Cancelling an NYT subscription does not automatically cancel a separate standalone Athletic plan.
steps.tip: If you upgraded from standalone Athletic to All Access, cancel the old standalone plan separately after confirming the bundle is active.

steps.title: Use Apple or Google Play for an app-store purchase
steps.text: A subscription purchased through iOS or Google Play must be cancelled with that third party. Save the store confirmation and check that the next renewal is gone.
steps.tip: Refund requests also go to the provider that processed the payment.

warnings: Cancelling a New York Times subscription does not automatically cancel a separately billed Athletic subscription.
Paid cancellations normally take effect at the end of the current subscription period. A cancellation during a free trial takes effect immediately under the current NYT terms.
Third-party purchases must be changed or cancelled through the same third party.
Old instructions that point only to theathletic.com/account may miss the current NYTimes account route.

faqs.q: Is The Athletic included with my New York Times plan?
faqs.a: The current NYT help page says All Access and Home Delivery include The Athletic. Check the What's included section in your Subscription Overview because plan availability can vary.

faqs.q: Why do I still see an Athletic charge after changing my NYT plan?
faqs.a: A standalone Athletic subscription can remain separate from the new bundle. Check the Athletic settings page and the merchant name on the receipt for a second renewal.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund from The Athletic?
faqs.a: Refund rights depend on the charge, billing provider, location, and timing. Contact NYT customer support for a direct charge. Apple or Google handles requests for purchases made through its store.

faqs.q: What happens to access after cancellation?
faqs.a: For a normal paid subscription, current NYT terms say access continues through the remainder of the subscription period. After that, subscriber-only coverage requires another eligible plan.

refund.details: A refund is not automatic. Use the provider on the receipt and include the payment date, cancellation confirmation, and any evidence of a duplicate or unexpected charge. Local consumer rights may add protections.

retentionTactics: The cancellation flow may show another subscription option or promotional price.
Check the final status instead of assuming that viewing an offer completed the cancellation.
